dedupe_keys.name: odin real time outages by county outage data initiative nationwide near real time utility outage reports us

description: The Outage Data Initiative Nationwide (ODIN), led by Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the US Department of Energy Office of Electricity, seeks a common digital reporting standard for power outage data so that utilities can exchange it freely with designated stakeholders. This Open Energy Hub dataset holds outage information provided by participating utilities in near-real time at county level. Fields include the utility name and identifier, county and state, incident identifier, cause and cause kind, incident location, meters affected, customers restored, status, reported start time and estimated restoration time, with county polygons from the US Census Bureau and centroids. The metadata showed 441 records and a last update on 26 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, with data processed as they change. Access is free and online through the Opendatasoft portal, with exports and an explore API and no sign-in. Coverage is the parts of the United States served by utilities that report to ODIN. Caveats: it is a live snapshot of current incidents from participating utilities only, not a national archive, no licence is stated, and the ODIN site itself returned only a title to automated reading. Simulation uses are live outage and restoration estimates for emergency response dashboards and for building restoration time distributions. Related records: data-eagle-i-recorded-electricity-outages-us-counties gives the historical county outage archive.
